title: When the Test Changes With the Room

questions.stem: The disease gets rarer. What falls?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity and specificity stay put. The room changes the predictive value.

questions.stem: As the disease gets common, a negative test:

options.text: Becomes a constant printed on the kit

questions.explanation: Negative predictive value falls as prevalence rises.

questions.stem: The chance you believed before the result is:

options.text: The pre-test probability, written down before you look

questions.explanation: The test revises that number. It does not create it.

options.text: Uses the misses, and does not contain prevalence
Is the same as the positive predictive value
Rises automatically when disease is rare

questions.explanation: It is one minus sensitivity, over specificity.

questions.stem: The preventive services task force recommends mammography:

options.text: Every other year from forty through seventy-four
Only after a palpable mass, as screening
Yearly from age twenty-one, as its only statement

questions.explanation: A palpable mass is a workup now, not a screening interval.

options.text: If there is bleeding after sex

questions.explanation: A vaccinated patient is still screened. Bleeding after sex is an exam now.

questions.stem: A very sensitive test that says yes in a rare disease:

options.text: May still be wrong most of the time

questions.explanation: False yeses crowd out the true ones when disease is rare.

options.text: Constants printed on every kit, in every room
Dependent on the population you are standing in

questions.explanation: Do the math in the room you are in.

questions.stem: A moderately sensitive test, used to exclude a dangerous disease:

options.text: Is a poor rule-out, because the negative likelihood ratio stays sizable

questions.explanation: The negative likelihood ratio uses the misses.
